hints.title: Problem Analysis
hints.text: Assign a unique row ID using ROW_NUMBER() to handle potential duplicate coordinate pairs.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Join the table with itself on p1.x = p2.y and p1.y = p2.x with different row IDs distinct row identifiers `p1.id <> p2.id`.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy
hints.text: Filter for unique pairs satisfying p1.x <= p1.y and sort by x, y ascending.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH P AS (
    SELECT ROW_NUMBER() OVER () AS id, X AS x, Y AS y 
    FROM Coordinates
)
SELECT DISTINCT p1.x, p1.y 
FROM P AS p1 
JOIN P AS p2 
  ON p1.x = p2.y 
 AND p1.y = p2.x 
 AND p1.x <= p1.y 
 AND p1.id != p2.id 
ORDER BY p1.x, p1.y;
```

import pandas as pd

def symmetric_coordinates(coordinates: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = coordinates.copy()
    df['id'] = range(len(df))
    merged = df.merge(df, left_on=['X', 'Y'], right_on=['Y', 'X'], suffixes=('_1', '_2'))
    res = merged[(merged['id_1'] != merged['id_2']) & (merged['X_1'] <= merged['Y_1'])][['X_1', 'Y_1']]
    res = res.drop_duplicates().sort_values(by=['X_1', 'Y_1']).rename(columns={'X_1': 'x', 'Y_1': 'y'})
    return res
